assumption: (a) each S2/S3 has at most one owner
evidence: 0 of 7,638,365 matched IDs appear under more than one S1

assumption: (b) names carry most of the signal
evidence: AUC name 0.976 vs address 0.956; true pairs agreeing on name only 10.1% vs address only 16.1%; name tsr<50 in 7.2%

assumption: (c) postal codes are reliable when present
evidence: a genuine code is on both records in only 0.16% of true pairs (n=321); they agree in 98.75% (6-digit 100.0% n=155; 5-digit 97.59% n=166). Naive digit-run matching agrees only 93.49% -- most 5/6-digit runs are house numbers.

assumption: (d) France shows the same noise patterns in a new language
evidence: 17/17 S2/S3-vs-S1 noise gaps in France point the same way as in the train countries (test split). Descriptive only: France has no labels.
